mainTopic: A lost גט that is later found: when we worry it belongs to another couple with the same names, and how the משנה fits with other sources about found documents.
overview: The משנה rules that if a שליח loses a גט, he may use it only if he finds it right away, finds it in a container he knows, or recognizes the גט itself. The גמרא raises a contradiction from a משנה in בבא מציעא, which suggests a found גט may be delivered even after a long time if the husband says 'give it.' רבה answers that our משנה is talking about a place where caravans (שיירות) often pass, so another man with the same name might have dropped the גט. The other משנה is talking about a place where caravans are rare. The גמרא adds that even where caravans are common, we only worry if two men with the same name are known to live in one town. It proves this from רבה's own ruling about a גט found in רב הונא's busy court, which he said should be returned. Then it tells of a real ruling רבה gave about a גט found in the flax house in פומבדיתא, and gives two versions of the details. Finally, רבי זירא sets our משנה against a ברייתא about a גט found in the marketplace, where returning it depends only on whether the husband agrees. The inference from that ברייתא and רבי זירא's answer continue on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה: a שליח who loses the גט
steps.stepSummary: A שליח who loses a גט may use it if he finds it right away. Otherwise it is invalid, unless he finds it in a known container or recognizes it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone is bringing a גט and loses it, there are two cases. If he finds it right away, it is valid. If not, it is invalid. If he finds it in a pouch or a box, or if he recognizes it, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the basic rule for a שליח who loses the גט on the way and then finds it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that the גט he found may not be the one he lost. It could belong to a different couple with the very same names. Finding it right away, finding it in a known container, or recognizing it removes that worry.
steps.confusionAlert: The problem here is not that the גט got damaged. The worry is that the found גט might be a different גט that only has the same names on it.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who brings a bill of divorce, and it was lost from him:
if he found it immediately, it is valid;
but if not, it is invalid.
If he found it in a pouch or in a box,
or if he recognizes it, it is valid.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lost גט is valid only if it is found immediately, found in a known container, or recognized. Otherwise it is invalid because it may belong to another couple with the same names.

steps.title: A contradiction from the משנה about found documents
steps.stepSummary: A משנה in בבא מציעא suggests that a found גט may be delivered even after a long time if the husband says 'give it.' This seems to contradict our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: They pointed out a contradiction. A משנה teaches: If someone finds a גט, a document freeing a slave, a will, a gift document, or a receipt, he should not return it. The reason is that perhaps they were written and the writer changed his mind about giving them. This implies that if the writer says 'give it,' we do give it, even after a long time!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another משנה and draws a conclusion from it that clashes with our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in בבא מציעא only worries that the writer changed his mind. It shows no worry about a second person with the same name. So once the writer says 'give it,' the found גט should be usable even after a long time. Our משנה, however, says it is invalid unless it was found right away.

keyTerms.meaning: And they contrasted it: introduces a contradiction between two sources

phrases.english: GEMARA: And they raised a contradiction:
phrases.notes: The source being quoted is a משנה in בבא מציעא 18a.

phrases.english: One who found bills of divorce of women, or documents freeing slaves,
wills, gift documents, or receipts,
this person should not return them,
because I say: they were written,
and he reconsidered about them, deciding not to give them.
This implies that if he said 'Give it,' we give it;
and even after a long time!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's ruling that a גט found after some time is invalid.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling in our משנה that a גט not found right away is invalid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה in בבא מציעא only worries that the writer changed his mind, not that someone else has the same name. That implies a found גט is fine even after a long time if the husband says to give it.

steps.title: רבה: it depends on whether caravans pass through
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that our משנה is talking about a place where caravans are common. The other משנה is talking about a place where they are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: There is no difficulty. This ruling is for a place where caravans are common. That ruling is for a place where caravans are not common.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה settles the contradiction by saying each משנה is talking about a different kind of place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where caravans (שיירות) often pass through, many travelers come by, so it is reasonable to fear the גט was dropped by someone else with the same name. That is why our משנה is strict. Where caravans are rare, there is no such fear, so the only worry is that the writer changed his mind, and that is solved when he says 'give it.'

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
Here... there: assigning each source to a different case

phrases.english: Rabba said: This is not difficult:
here, it is in a place where caravans are common;
phrases.notes: "Here" is our משנה, which is strict about a lost גט.

phrases.english: there, it is in a place where caravans are not common.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source is assigned to a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two משניות seemed to give opposite rules for the same found גט.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה applies where many travelers pass through and a same-name גט is possible. The משנה in בבא מציעא applies where travelers are rare.

steps.title: Only when two men with the same name are known in town
steps.stepSummary: Even where caravans are common, we only worry if two men with the same name are known to live in that one town.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even in a place where caravans are common, the worry only applies when it is known that there are two men named יוסף בן שמעון in one town.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows רבה's answer. It tells us exactly when the worry about a mix-up actually applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Caravans being common is not enough by itself to invalidate the found גט. The fear of a mix-up only applies if there are known to be two people with identical names in that town. Without that, the גט can still be used.

keyTerms.meaning: And that is only when...: introduces a limiting condition
It was established, it is known

steps.whatToRemember: A found גט is invalid (unless found right away or recognized) only when there is a real chance of a mix-up: caravans are common AND two men with the same name are known in that town.

phrases.english: And even in a place where caravans are common,

phrases.aramaic: וְהוּא שֶׁהוּחְזְקוּ שְׁנֵי יוֹסֵף בֶּן שִׁמְעוֹן
phrases.english: that is only when it was established that two men named Yosef ben Shimon live
in one town.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבה's answer by adding a further condition before the worry applies.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The worry of a same-name mix-up applies only where caravans are common and two men with the same name are known to live in that town.

steps.title: If not, רבה would contradict himself: the גט found in רב הונא's court
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a proof for Step 4. It brings a case of a גט found in רב הונא's court, where רב הונא worried there might be two towns named שוירי.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you don't agree that we only worry when two people with the same name are known, then רבה contradicts himself. A גט was found in רב הונא's court. It said it was written in 'שוירי, the town on the רכיס river.' רב הונא said: we worry there may be two towns named שוירי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a proof that the rule in Step 4 is correct. It starts telling a story that will show what רבה really holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim is that without Step 4's rule, two of רבה's rulings would clash. This step only sets the scene. רב הונא raises a worry that there might be a second town with the same name, so the גט could belong to someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: A contradiction between one statement of רבה and another statement of רבה
We are concerned / we take the possibility into account

phrases.english: For if you do not say so,
phrases.notes: He means: if you don't accept Step 4's rule, that we only worry when two people with the same name are known.

phrases.english: there is a contradiction between Rabba and Rabba:
for there was a certain bill of divorce that was found
in the court of Rav Huna,
and it was written in it:
"In Sheviri, the town that is on the Rakhis River,"
and Rav Huna said:
We are concerned that there may be two towns called Sheviri;

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי לָא תֵּימָא הָכִי, קַשְׁיָא דְּרַבָּה אַדְּרַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a proof supporting the conclusion of Step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That רבה only worries about a same-name mix-up when two such people are known to exist in one town.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The incident of the גט found in רב הונא's court, together with רבה's ruling about it.

steps.title: רבה finds a משנה: court documents are returned
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא sends רבה to research the question. רבה finds a משנה that all court documents are returned to their owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא told רבה: Go look into this, because tonight רב הונא will ask you about it. רבה went out, looked carefully, and found that we learned in a משנה: All court documents should be returned.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. רבה researches the question and finds a משנה that says court documents found are given back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not worry that the document might belong to someone else with the same name. רבה uses this to rule that the גט in רב הונא's court should be returned. This is the ruling the גמרא will build its proof on.

keyTerms.meaning: Go out and look into it
Court documents (documents the court has dealt with)

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda said to Rabba:
Go out and look into it,

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְאוּרְתָּא בָּעֵי לַהּ מִינָּךְ רַב הוּנָא.
phrases.english: for tonight Rav Huna will ask you about it.
He went out, examined carefully, and found:
As we learned in a mishnah:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מַעֲשֵׂה בֵּית דִּין – הֲרֵי זֶה יַחְזִיר.
phrases.english: All court documents: one should return them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא לְרַבָּה: פּוֹק וְעַיֵּין בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבה's answer to the case of the גט found in רב הונא's court.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's ruling that the found גט should be returned.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: כל מעשה בית דין הרי זה יחזיר.

steps.title: So רבה only worries when two same-name people are known
steps.stepSummary: A court is a busy place, like a place where caravans are common, yet רבה ruled to return the document. So he must only worry when two people with the same name are known.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב הונא's court is like a place where caravans are common, and still רבה ruled 'return it.' So clearly: if two men named יוסף בן שמעון are known to live in one town, yes, we worry. If not, we don't.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof. It shows that the only way to make sense of רבה's ruling is the rule from Step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 3 רבה said that where caravans are common, a found גט is not returned. A court is full of people coming and going, so it is like that kind of place, yet רבה said to return the document. The contradiction disappears only if being in a busy place isn't enough, and we also need two people with the same name to be known in one town.

keyTerms.meaning: Caravans are common (lots of travelers pass through)
He ruled / he resolved the question
It was established / it is known

steps.whatToRemember: רבה's full position: we worry that a found גט belongs to someone else only if caravans are common there and two men with the same name are known to live in one town.

phrases.english: But the court of Rav Huna,
is like a place where caravans are common,
and yet he ruled "one should return it";
phrases.notes: "He" is רבה, who found the משנה in the last step.

phrases.english: Apparently,

phrases.aramaic: אִי הוּחְזְקוּ שְׁנֵי יוֹסֵף בֶּן שִׁמְעוֹן בְּעִיר אַחַת – אִין,
phrases.english: if two men named Yosef ben Shimon are known to be in one town, yes, we are concerned,
and if not, we are not concerned.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא בֵּי דִינָא דְּרַב הוּנָא, דְּכִמְקוֹם שֶׁהַשַּׁיָּירוֹת מְצוּיוֹת דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from רבה's ruling in Step 6, completing the proof that began in Step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Even where caravans are common, we only worry about a same-name mix-up if two such people are known to live in one town. This confirms Step 4.

steps.title: רבה rules on a גט found in a flax house in פומבדיתא
steps.stepSummary: רבה gave a practical ruling, following his own teaching, about a גט found in the flax house in פומבדיתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה made an actual ruling about a גט that was found in the flax house in פומבדיתא, following his own teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case where רבה applied his rule. This step sets up the next lines, which explain the details of where the גט was found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that רבה's rule was used in practice and not only discussed. The details that decide the case come in the next two steps, which give two different versions.

keyTerms.meaning: He made a practical ruling in a real case

phrases.english: Rabba made a practical ruling
regarding a certain bill of divorce
that was found in the flax house in Pumbedita,
according to his teaching.
phrases.notes: His teaching means his rule about caravans and two people with the same name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After proving רבה's rule, the גמרא shows him applying it in a real case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה ruled on a found גט in פומבדיתא according to his own rule.

steps.title: First version: where flax was soaked, so caravans were not common
steps.stepSummary: Some say the גט was found where flax is soaked. Even though two people with the same name were known, the גט was valid because caravans don't pass there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it was in the place where they soak flax. Even though two people with the same name were known, the גט was returned because caravans are not common there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first version of where the גט was found. It shows the case fit רבה's first condition, from Step 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, one condition for worrying was there: two people with the same name were known. But the other condition was missing, because travelers don't pass by the flax-soaking place. Since both conditions are needed, there was nothing to worry about.

phrases.english: Some say
it was in the place where they soak flax,
and even though it was known that there were two people with the same name,
the bill of divorce was valid, since caravans are not common there;

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי בְּדוּכְתָּא הֵיכָא דְּתָרוּ כִּיתָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the details of רבה's ruling from Step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Where caravans are not common, a found גט is valid even if two people with the same name are known.

steps.title: Second version: where flax was sold, but no two same-name people were known
steps.stepSummary: Others say the גט was found where flax is sold and caravans are common. It was valid because two people with the same name were not known.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say it was in the place where they sell flax. The גט was valid because two people with the same name were not known, even though caravans are common there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the same case. This time it fits רבה's second condition, from Step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the busy-place condition was there, because the flax market draws travelers. But no two people with the same name were known, so the other condition was missing. Either way, the גט was valid, and each version shows one half of רבה's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Provided that it was not / and it was not

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions of רבה's flax-house ruling end the same way: the גט is valid. Each version shows that one condition alone, a busy place or a known same name, is not enough to make us worry.
steps.confusionAlert: The two versions do not disagree about the הלכה. They only disagree about which detail of the case made the גט valid.

phrases.english: And some say
it was in the place where they sell flax,
and it was not known that there were two people with the same name,
even though caravans are common there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different version of the details of the case in Step 8, instead of the version in Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Where caravans are common, a found גט is still valid if two people with the same name are not known.

steps.title: רבי זירא introduces a contradiction and quotes the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא is introduced as someone who raised a contradiction between the משנה and a ברייתא and also resolved it. The גמרא first quotes the משנה: a שליח who lost a גט may use it only if he found it right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא pointed out a contradiction between the משנה and a ברייתא, and then answered it. We learned in the משנה: if someone is bringing a גט and loses it, then if he finds it right away it is valid, and if not, it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new question. It tells us that רבי זירא will compare two sources, and it quotes the first one, our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה makes timing the deciding factor. Find the lost גט right away and it is כשר; find it later and it is פסול. This rule is the first side of the contradiction that is about to be raised.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises a contradiction (literally, 'throws' two sources against each other)
A teaching from the time of the משנה that was not included in the משנה
'We learned', the phrase used to quote a משנה

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira raises a contradiction between the Mishnah and a baraita,
and he answers it.
We learned: one who brings a get, and it was lost from him,
if he found it immediately, it is valid,
and if not, it is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי זֵירָא רָמֵי מַתְנִיתִין אַבָּרַיְיתָא, וּמְשַׁנֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new line of discussion about lost גיטין, approached through a contradiction between two sources.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the משנה, a lost גט is valid only if it is found right away.

steps.title: The ברייתא about a גט found in the marketplace
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. If someone finds a גט in the marketplace and the husband agrees he gave it, the finder returns it to the wife. If the husband does not agree, it is returned to no one. The גמרא then starts to draw an inference from this.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he contrasted it with a ברייתא: if someone found a woman's גט in the marketplace, then when the husband agrees, he should return it to the woman. If the husband does not agree, he should not return it to either one of them. So we can learn from here...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the second source, a ברייתא, to set against the משנה. At the very end it begins to point out what this ברייתא implies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, what decides the case is whether the husband agrees, and it says nothing about finding the גט right away. This seems to clash with the משנה, which makes timing the deciding factor. The word הָא opens the inference that will show the clash clearly.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he contrasted them', which brings a source that seems to contradict the first one
In the marketplace, a public place where many people pass
Agrees, admits (here: that he wrote and gave the גט)
'But this implies...', which opens an inference

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume the ברייתא is talking about finding the גט right away. The point is that it never mentions timing, and that silence is exactly what creates the contradiction.

phrases.english: And he raised a contradiction:
If one found a woman's get in the marketplace,
when the husband admits, he should return it to the woman;
if the husband does not admit,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יַחְזִיר לֹא לָזֶה וְלֹא לָזֶה.
phrases.english: he should not return it, not to this one and not to that one.
phrases.notes: Meaning neither to the husband nor to the wife.

phrases.english: But (this implies)...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the second source, which seems to contradict the משנה quoted in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that a lost גט is valid only if it is found right away.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא makes returning the גט depend only on whether the husband agrees, without requiring that it be found right away. That suggests a גט found later could also be valid.
